title: DFlash: Block Diffusion for Flash Speculative Decoding
anchored_claims: DFlash uses a lightweight block diffusion draft model to generate speculative draft tokens in parallel, conditioned on hidden features extracted from the target LLM (Figure 2).
On Qwen3 models with thinking disabled, DFlash consistently outperforms EAGLE-3 and reaches about 4.9x average greedy-decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding (Table 1).
With thinking mode enabled, DFlash maintains high acceptance length and roughly 4.5x speedups on reasoning-model settings (Table 2).
On SGLang with the FA4 backend, DFlash provides throughput speedups across Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct up to 5.1x (Table 3).
Long-context fine-tuning preserves or improves DFlash acceptance length as LongBench context length increases beyond 4K (Table 4).
Ablations show that draft depth, number of target hidden features, block-size choice, and KV injection all materially affect DFlash acceptance length and speedup (Table 6; Table 7; Table 8; Table 9).
